title: Microrefactor roadmap and safety checks
content:
Purpose
----
This is a personal scratchpad for planning small, low-risk refactors (microrefactors) in the serving runtime. Goal: make a repeatable checklist + rollout recipe so I (and anyone else) can do fast changes without causing instability. Keep notes, quick experiments, and follow-ups here.

Context & constraints
- Changes targeted: single-file or small-module refactors (<= 250 LOC changed), no schema changes, no consumer-facing API contract updates.
- Typical risk vectors: thread-safety assumptions, KV-cache invalidation, batching loop behavior, and cold-start path.
- Required: unit tests + focused integration smoke, canary on dedicated pool with traffic shaping, clear rollback plan.

Microrefactor categories (examples)
- Local algorithm tidy (rename, extract helper)
- Performance tweak (early-exit in hot path, reduce allocations)
- Observability addition (span tags, metric increments)
- Small concurrency change (convert Mutex -> RwLock within constrained boundary)

Pre-PR checklist (fast gate to open a PR)
- [ ] Short PR description: one-sentence intent + list of expected runtime effects (latency, memory)
- [ ] Linked ticket (ENG- or MISC-) or note explaining why this matters now
- [ ] Tests added/updated: unit + 1 integration scenario (happy path)
- [ ] Local repro steps included in PR description (how to run the failing case locally)
- [ ] Bench snippet (if perf change): before/after numbers, command used to measure
- [ ] Owner & reviewer assigned (owner != reviewer)

PR review heuristics (what I look for)
- Code size: if >250 LOC changed, escalate to medium refactor checklist
- Critical paths: is change touching request hot path? If yes, ensure micro-bench or perf artifacts
- Concurrency: check for non-atomic read-modify-write patterns; look for map/vec mutation under shared ownership
- Error handling: are errors correctly propagated or swallowed? Add tests for error cases
- Observability: add at least one metric or log that helps debug the change in production (counter/gauge or debug trace)

Local quick tests (commands)
- unit: cargo test module::test_name --release
- integration: ./scripts/run-smoke.sh --scenario small-batch
- perf quick: ./bench/latency.sh --requests 200 --concurrency 8 (note before/after numbers in PR)

Canary & rollout plan (for hosted/dedicated)
1) Canary environment: deploy to canary pool with 2-4 GPUs, route 2% traffic for 30 minutes.
2) Metrics to watch (real-time dashboard names):
   - token_latency.p50/p95/p99  (alert if p95 increases > 15% of baseline)
   - request_errors.rate (alert if > 0.5% new errors over baseline)
   - cpu/gpu_utilization (large delta may indicate busy loop)
   - kv_cache_hit_rate (if change touches caching logic)
   - memory_resident_ratio (alert if > +200 MB per instance)
3) Canary duration: 30–90 minutes depending on traffic pattern. If all good, expand to 10% for 60 minutes, then 50% for 30m, full.
4) Quick smoke test after each expansion: curl health endpoint on a few instances and run a deterministic prompt to ensure result shape unchanged.

Rollback recipe (fast path)
- Immediate revert via console deploy (tagged rollback) and route all traffic to previous model/variant.
- If console unavailable: scale down canary pool and scale up baseline pool (kubectl / terraform shortcuts documented below).
- Postmortem steps: collect logs, trace samples, and perf bench; open incident note with timeline + blame-free analysis.

Post-merge follow-ups (1–2 days)
- [ ] Add a test asserting specific invariant uncovered during PR review
- [ ] Sweep for similar code patterns across repo and file follow-up TODOs
- [ ] Add a quick eval harness if change is about output normalization (run small prompt suite)

Safety kernels (quick snippets I paste often)
- Defensive check for optional pointer: if let Some(x) = opt { use(x) } else { return Err(…) }
- Atomic swap: let old = std::mem::replace(&mut shared.foo, new_val); assert!(old != new_val || fallback());
- KV-cache safe update: clone-on-write pattern with Arc + RwLock read-then-write path documented

Example PR description template (to copy):
"Short summary: remove double-lock in batching loop to avoid redundant contention. Expected effect: reduce p95 tail by ~5-10% for small-batch workloads, no API change.
Why now: observed in production traces (trace-ids: abc..).
How tested: unit tests + local micro-benchmark (command). Canary plan: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with metrics above. Rollback: console tag rollback.
Files touched: runtime/batching.rs (120 LOC), runtime/lock_helpers.rs (30 LOC)."

Open questions / TODO items
- Can we standardize a single small-bench script for all microrefactors? (leah asked about this 2024-11)
- Add a template for perf artifacts upload to GH comment (so reviewers don't have to download from CI)
- Should microrefactors require two reviewers if touching hot path? (propose: yes when touching batching or cache)

Misc notes (scratch)
- Quick warmup trick: run a 2-instance local cluster with smaller batch size to reproduce tail latency spikes.
- If changing locks, always run under thread sanitizer locally (where possible) or a small stress test for 5 minutes on staging.
- Keep PRs focused: if you find a second refactor while working, file a follow-up PR unless trivial rename.

History of small follow-ups from this doc
- 2024-12-05: added canary thresholds after incident with KV cache invalidation.
- 2024-12-18: added perf snippet and template.

If you use anything in here, ping me in slack (ashoka) so I can iterate the checklist based on real-world pain points.
